group_assessment.weighting: Measured 2026-09-13 by PubMed esearch: 'Aldaz CM[Author]' = 138, 'Aldaz CM[Author] AND WWOX' = 38, 'Ludes-Meyers JH[Author]' = 13. This is the laboratory that cloned WWOX and it is the primary group FOR THE GENE — the reagent, the physical map and the tumour-suppressor phenotype all originate here. It is NOT primary for the disease: nothing here concerns a neurodevelopmental phenotype and WWOX-DEE did not exist as a described entity in 2003. The reweighting is therefore asymmetric and that asymmetry is the point. OBSERVATION weighs high: on what immunogen its own antiserum was raised, this group is the most authoritative source that can exist, because it made the reagent. INTERPRETATION weighs low and is in places self-interested: the same paper asserts the sex-steroid function it had itself hypothesised, draws a 'necessary and sufficient' conclusion whose sufficiency leg is 'data not shown', and states in its abstract as established a PPXY result its own body calls preliminary and in preparation.

field_density.reading: The two queries that matter to this lot return 1 and 2. entries.proposition: The immunogen for the anti-WWOX antiserum is stated once and unambiguously: a GST fusion to WWOX residues 12-94 spanning both WW domains. This single sentence reconciles rather than adjudicates the two different immunogen descriptions given by the later papers that cite this one for characterisation, because a GST-WWOX fusion protein and 'the WW domains' are two true descriptions of one immunogen.

what_this_reading_does_not_establish: It does not establish any immunohistochemical validity for the anti-WWOX antiserum. The article contains no immunohistochemistry, no immunostaining, no tissue section and no fixation of any kind: 'immunohistochem' occurs 0 times, 'immunostain' 0, 'isotype' 0, 'pre-immune' 0, 'pre-absor' 0.

It does not establish that the antiserum is mono-specific: a residual higher-molecular-weight band is visible in the WWOX-null lane and in every lane of both blots, and no control in the paper characterises it.
It does not establish the ~46 kDa identity on the panel that asserts it, because Fig. 5A carries no molecular-weight ladder; 'ladder' and 'molecular weight marker' occur 0 times.
It does not establish that the reagent distinguishes full-length WWOX from SDR-deleted isoforms — the paper states the opposite, by design.
It does not establish a sex-steroid enzymatic function: nothing hormonal or enzymatic is measured.
It does not establish that the SDR domain is sufficient for Golgi localisation: that leg is 'data not shown'.
It does not establish the PPXY ligand result, which the body calls preliminary and in preparation while the abstract states it as fact.
It does not quantify the xenograft effect: no n, no test, no p-value.
It establishes nothing about a neurodevelopmental phenotype, about CNS tissue, or about the reference genotype. This is a 2003 cancer-genetics review and WWOX-DEE lies entirely outside it.
